posts.content_md:
I was doing some thought experiments in my hotel room and came up with the following idea:

Has anyone ever tried to expose a mold coated DCG hologram BEFORE separating the mold plate? I calculated that before separating the plates and exposing at Brewsters, fringe planes would be at a distance of about 352nm apart. If the thickness of the mold is 60um and after separating the plates and drying, the thickness becomes 12um, the new fringes will be about 153nm apart and slanted at about 24 degrees.

- At Bragg angle, this hologram would reflect light at about 306nm. 

- BUT: Light that reflects off every other fringe would intefere back at 612nm.

So, I guess that my question is: Can a Bragg condition be fulfilled with light bouncing off every other fringe instead of every subsequent fringe?

It would be very beneficial if this would work with MBDCG because of higher sensitivity in very wet emulsions and because of much greated environmental stability while still inside the mold.

posts.content_md: Hans, if you take a finished hologram that replays in the green, let's say 532, and illuminate it with infrared at 1064 does the infrared hologram show up? Or...you really don't have to see the infrared hologram, just study the IR light that goes through the hologram and subtract the potential DE of the reflected IR light if there is any.

posts.content_md:
Thank you for that suggestion. Unfortunately I don't have a source of 1064nm light. 

But your suggestion does perhaps lead to a question that answers part of this puzzle: If this system could work, then how do nd:YVO4 crystal makers produce coatings on their crystals that are HR for 1064nm and HT for 533nm at the same time?

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
> how do nd:YVO4 crystal makers produce coatings on their crystals that are HR for 1064nm and HT for 533nm at the same time?

You may be overthinking this one. If a coating is HR for 1064 then it is probably HT for all other wavelengths. So one HR coating for 1064 would be all that is needed.
